Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A records office maintains structured ledgers of component transactions and maintenance actions. Each document bears a unique serial, a date stamp, and an authorized signature block. Records move through defined routing channels, and final status changes require verification of the preceding entries before the file is archived.

2) What occurred: On 14 March 2023, the actor entered a substitute part identifier into the inventory ledger, field C-14, without verifying the source certificate; the source certificate check remained unverified. On 14 March 2023, the actor modified the installation date in the maintenance log, field M-22, to align with the substitute entry; the date consistency check remained unverified. On 15 March 2023, the actor signed the airworthiness release form, document AR-09, using a second named account; the second signature authorization remained unverified. On 16 March 2023, the actor forwarded the updated file through channel R-4 to the external regulator mailbox; the external receipt confirmation remained unverified.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor accessed the maintenance database using a named administrative account. The actor utilized a digital signature tool associated with a second named account. The actor utilized a standard PDF editor to alter document AR-09.

4) Indicators & artifacts: The inventory ledger shows a mismatch between part identifier C-14 and the original source certificate. The maintenance log displays a timestamp anomaly in field M-22. The airworthiness release form AR-09 contains a signature hash inconsistent with the primary account. The email log for channel R-4 shows an outbound message without a corresponding internal review ticket.
